tone_patterns: Formal, institutional tone that frames sustainability as integral to business strategy and value creation
Forward-looking language balanced with present-tense statements of integration and commitment
Stakeholder-oriented phrasing that links actions to outcomes and accountability
Standards- and framework-referential tone to signal alignment with external expectations
Measured, report-like cadence using clear topic sentences followed by supporting detail
paragraph_patterns: Opens with a short overview paragraph positioning sustainability as embedded across culture, operations, and planning
Uses sequential paragraphs that move from strategy intent → alignment to frameworks → governance/materiality linkage → thematic pillars
Employs short paragraphs with one main idea each, often starting with a declarative statement and then adding rationale
Introduces lists after a lead-in sentence (e.g., eligible categories, initiatives) to improve scanability
Uses recurring ‘commitment + mechanism + outcome’ structure (commitment stated, mechanism described, outcome/benefit referenced)
Transitions between themes using mini-narratives that explain why the theme matters and how it is operationalized
Closes subsections with reinforcement statements tying back to materiality, stakeholder priorities, or measurable outcomes
heading_patterns: Section numbering hierarchy: major section number + title, followed by decimal sub-section numbering (e.g., 3.1) with a concise label
Subsection headings are short nouns/phrases (e.g., “Overview”) rather than full sentences
Repeated running header/footer label of the section title appears on subsequent pages for orientation
Theme titles are presented as standalone labels (often in a row/column layout) to act as anchors for the content that follows
table_patterns: Matrix-style presentation mapping ‘focus themes’ across columns with consistent row types (e.g., Achievement / Target / Focus)
Each theme column uses the same internal structure and bullet formatting to enable comparison
Row labels (Achievement, Target, Focus) are visually distinct and repeated identically across themes
Bullets within cells use short fragments; sub-bullets use indented dashes to show hierarchy
Table functions as a strategy-at-a-glance summary before deeper narrative elaboration in subsequent pages
figure_or_diagram_patterns: Strategy themes are treated as a visual set (a labeled lineup) that can be reused as a diagrammatic ‘pillars’ device
Use of compact callouts within the matrix (Achievement/Target/Focus) to mimic infographic behavior without heavy graphics
Numbered theme list is repeated later as a recap device, acting like a lightweight diagram/legend
pdf_layout_patterns: Multi-page section with a dedicated section opener page showing a large section number and title
Consistent running header with the section name on content pages
Footer includes page number and report title line; layout supports quick navigation
Two-stage layout: (1) overview narrative page(s) → (2) strategy themes matrix page → (3) expanded narrative by theme
Use of whitespace and short line lengths to maintain readability; frequent line breaks and paragraph spacing
Bulleted lists are left-aligned with hanging indents; sub-bullets are indented further using dash markers
Occasional repetition of theme list at page end to reinforce structure and aid scanning
disclosure_language_patterns: Uses alignment language to connect strategy to external frameworks and national/international agendas without over-explaining them
References materiality assessment as the basis for prioritization and as a governance/strategy linkage
Uses ‘transparency and accountability’ phrasing to justify reporting outputs (e.g., impact reporting, disclosure enhancements)
Separates ‘what we aim to do’ (targets/intent) from ‘what we did’ (achievements/actions) using explicit labels
Uses cautious, non-absolute phrasing when describing future plans (e.g., planned, scheduled, aims to)
evidence_presentation_patterns: Evidence is presented in three tiers: headline recognition/ratings (credibility signals), reporting outputs (process evidence), and operational initiatives (implementation evidence)
Quantitative evidence is grouped under ‘Achievement’ and ‘Target’ labels to avoid mixing past performance with forward-looking statements
Uses examples of eligible categories/projects to substantiate claims without detailing every initiative
Mentions publication of reports/assurance as evidence of disclosure maturity
Connects evidence back to stakeholder relevance via materiality references
section_specific_observations: Strategy section is organized around a small set of named focus themes that recur across pages and formats (narrative, matrix, recap list)
The section blends strategic intent with operationalization by pairing thematic pillars with concrete mechanisms (frameworks, tools, reporting, initiatives)
The matrix acts as the central organizing artifact; subsequent narrative paragraphs expand each theme in turn
Lists of eligible categories and initiatives are used to make abstract strategy tangible while staying high-level
things_to_avoid_copying: Any company name, brand/program names, or proprietary initiative titles
Any specific awards, rankings, or third-party rating outcomes
Any numeric achievements, targets, dates, or time-bound commitments as written
Any named external tools/vendors or implementation partners
Any country/region-specific policy references or national agenda names
Any claims of being ‘first’ or ‘highest’ in a region/industry
Any specific stakeholder counts, website traffic figures, or engagement metrics
Any detailed product/service descriptions that could identify the reference organization
content_specific_items_detected_and_excl: Awards program names and award categories
Specific sustainability finance amounts and targets
Net-zero year commitment and interim reduction percentages
Specific reporting frameworks and report publication claims tied to particular years
Named ESG rating providers and ranking statements
Named technology platform/vendor and planned chatbot deployment timeline
Specific stakeholder visitation metrics and website references
Named pledge/council references and representation targets with dates
